title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 37
paragraphs: When the building of the bridges had been finished, and the works about Athos — both the embankments built around the mouths of the channel (so that the surf beating on the beach would not silt them up) and the channel itself — were reported to be fully completed, then, after wintering at Sardis, the army set forth from there fully equipped at the beginning of spring, to march to Abydos. As it was just setting out, the sun left its place in the sky and was invisible, though there was no gathering of clouds and the sky was perfectly clear; and instead of day it became night. When Xerxes saw and took notice of this, it became a matter of concern to him, and he asked the Magi what the appearance portended. They answered that the god was foreshowing to the Greeks the abandoning of their cities, for the sun, they said, was the foreshower of events for the Greeks, but the moon for the Persians. Thus informed, Xerxes proceeded on the march in very great good cheer.
